messages:
maya: opening a small docs PR that standardizes the airgapped installer preflight UX for USB-based mirror installs. goal: concise checklist + one-liner commands, USB mounting example, and a short policy blurb about allowed devices. PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1288 :clipboard:
felix: love it. can we add a tiny preflight script that verifies manifest signature and verifies that only signed packages are present? ops asked for an explicit exit code behavior so automation can rely on it.
rachel: also add a short policy paragraph: only approved, scanned USBs allowed for regulated installs, and an example sentence ops can copy to their compliance docs. mention that block devices should be mounted read-only during verification.
dmitri: include a short python SDK example showing the installer attempting control-plane KMS and then a local signature-verify fallback. keep the SDK example as a single snippet and non-opinionated.
maya: plan: 1) preflight-check.sh one-liner + example output 2) mount/read-only systemd unit 3) manifest gpg verify example 4) python snippet for fallback 5) policy blurb + troubleshooting bullets 6) linkcheck to the security policy doc
felix: preflight script idea (short):
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e
MOUNT=/mnt/usbrepo
mkdir -p $MOUNT
mount -o ro /dev/disk/by-label/REDWOOD_USB $MOUNT
# verify manifest signature
gpg --keyring /etc/redwood/trusted-keys.gpg --verify $MOUNT/manifest.sig $MOUNT/manifest.json || exit 2
# verify all tarballs listed in manifest exist and checksum
jq -r '.files[] | "\(.path) \(.sha256)"' $MOUNT/manifest.json | while read -r path sha; do
  sha256sum -c <(echo "$sha  $MOUNT/$path") || exit 3
done
echo "PRELIGHT_OK"
exit 0
```
rachel: add the systemd unit for mounting read-only and ensuring the preflight runs before installer starts:
```ini
[Unit]
Description=Mount USB repo read-only and run preflight
After=local-fs.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/bin/mkdir -p /mnt/usbrepo
ExecStart=/bin/mount -o ro /dev/disk/by-label/REDWOOD_USB /mnt/usbrepo
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/preflight-check.sh
RemainAfterExit=yes

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```
dmitri: python SDK fallback (tiny):
```python
# redwood-py: try online KMS, fallback to local verification
from redwood import KMSClient
import subprocess

kms = KMSClient(endpoint="https://kms.private.example")
try:
    kms.validate_node()
except Exception:
    # offline: run manifest verify script
    r = subprocess.run(["/usr/local/bin/preflight-check.sh"]) 
    if r.returncode != 0:
        raise SystemExit("preflight failed: " + str(r.returncode))
print("preflight ok")
```
felix: troubleshooting bullets to add: - exit code 2 -> signature verify failed (wrong key or tampered) - exit code 3 -> checksum mismatch (incomplete copy) - mount failure -> device label mismatch or permission issue. Also note SELinux and mount namespaces can block mount.
maya: policy blurb draft: "For regulated private installs, only OS-validated images and operator-approved removable media are permitted. Operators must scan and sign mirror bundles in an approved build environment. Removable media must be mounted read-only and validated before installer execution." I'll add a one-line copy-paste for customers.
rachel: tiny UX note: make the installer preflight output machine-parseable JSON in addition to human-friendly logs so automation can surface clear failure reasons. add example output: `{"status":"error","code":3,"detail":"checksum mismatch: pkg-1234.tar.gz"}`.
dmitri: also mention token TTL caveat: cached tokens used for short-lived operations only; if the cached cert/token has expired, the preflight should fail with explicit code and guidance. include a link to the token TTL docs page.
infra-bot: lint: docs PR 1288 queued for linkcheck and spellcheck. :gear:
felix: reviewer checklist: 1) run preflight script with a tampered manifest and confirm exit code 2) run preflight with a valid signed manifest and confirm PRELIGHT_OK output 3) verify systemd unit ordering prevents installer from starting on failure 4) confirm JSON error output shape for automation 5) confirm compliance policy blurb reads clearly for regulated customers
